description.en:
Not a function a script can call: an identifier of the game's message (dialogue text) parser.
It exists only as a symbol string in the game's ELF binary, lxpCMessage::DATA::CMND_CHAR. That makes it a value of an enum named DATA inside the lxpCMessage class, the list of control codes the parser recognises inside message text.
Going by its name, it stands for a plain text character. The byte-level encoding in the message files was not traced.
The fifteen names of that enum appear together in the binary in this order: CMND_NONE, CMND_CHAR, CMND_CHAR_RUBI, CMND_RUBI, CMND_RUBI_END, CMND_GAIJI, CMND_LINE, CMND_WAIT, CMND_TOUCH_WAIT, CMND_SKIP_START, CMND_SKIP_END, CMND_COLOR_START, CMND_COLOR_END, CMND_COLOR_RUBI_START, CMND_COLOR_RUBI_END. CMND_CHAR is number 1 in that list, which is probably its enum value (not confirmed).
It is not registered as a Squirrel function and appears nowhere in the shipped scripts.
Not applicable: this is not a callable function. Calling CMND_CHAR from a script would fail because no such global exists.
